title: A paused holder, fenced out
request:
c1 takes the lock and stalls, the lease expires, c2 takes it and writes

./your_program.sh fencing
acquire c1
expire
acquire c2
write c2 2 v2
write c1 1 v1
state
note: c1 is not misbehaving: from its own point of view it holds the lock and is writing exactly once. Nothing it can check tells it otherwise, because the pause happened after the check. Only the resource, comparing token 1 against a fence of 2, is in a position to notice.

title: The same story with no fence
request:
the identical sequence against a resource that does not check tokens

./your_program.sh fencing
acquire c1
expire
acquire c2
write-unfenced c2 v2
write-unfenced c1 v1
state
note: This is the failure the pattern exists to prevent, and it is silent: no error is reported anywhere, the lock service behaved correctly throughout, and the data is simply wrong afterwards.
